questions.question: You need 500 hosts in one subnet. Smallest traditional IPv4 mask that fits (ignoring special cases)?
options: /23 (512 addresses, 510 usable in classic host math)—/24 is only 254 usable
questions.explanation: CIDR sizing: powers of two; leave headroom.

questions.question: Two routes 10.0.0.0/8 and 10.1.2.0/24 exist. Packet to 10.1.2.9 uses:
options: Longest Prefix Match — the /24 wins over the /8
questions.explanation: LPM is the core of IP forwarding.

questions.question: ARP maps:
options: IPv4 address to MAC address on a local L2 segment
questions.explanation: Fundamentals: control plane for Ethernet last hop.

questions.question: Classic symptom of MTU black hole:
options: Large packets fail (often when DF set) while small pings work—path MTU discovery issues
questions.explanation: MTU/PMTUD is a Dive Deep favorite.

questions.question: TTL/hop limit exists to:
options: Bound packet lifetime and kill loops—traceroute increments TTL to map paths

questions.question: RIB vs FIB:
options: RIB is the routing table(s) from protocols; FIB is the forwarding table installed for data plane lookups

questions.question: ECMP at L3 means:
options: Multiple equal-cost next hops; flow hashing spreads traffic

questions.question: Broadcast domain vs subnet:
options: A subnet is an L3 addressing construct; a broadcast domain is L2 reach without a router—design should align them carefully
They are always the same globally

questions.question: Underlay vs overlay:
options: Underlay forwards the outer transport; overlay (VXLAN/VPN/etc.) carries tenant networks atop it

questions.question: traceroute typically works by:
options: Sending probes with increasing TTL and reading ICMP time-exceeded from hops

questions.question: Anycast in networking means:
options: Same prefix announced from multiple places; routing delivers to a 'near' instance

questions.question: Unicast vs multicast vs broadcast:
options: Unicast one-to-one; multicast one-to-group; broadcast one-to-all on a segment
Broadcast works across the Internet by default

questions.question: A default route 0.0.0.0/0 means:
options: Gateway of last resort when no more-specific route matches

questions.question: NAT typically breaks which assumption?
options: End-to-end addressing transparency—ports/addresses rewritten; some apps need helpers or avoid NAT

questions.question: TCP vs UDP manager-level:
options: TCP is reliable, ordered, connection-oriented; UDP is datagram, no built-in reliability—choose per app needs

questions.question: ICMP is primarily:
options: Control/error messaging for IP (unreachable, time exceeded, echo)—not a data transport for apps

questions.question: Ethernet switches forward unknown unicast by:
options: Flooding within the VLAN/broadcast domain while learning source MACs from frames

questions.question: Duplex mismatch classic symptom:
options: Poor performance, late collisions/errors on one side—verify speed/duplex on copper links

questions.question: If L2 FCS is fine but app data corrupt, consider:
options: Higher-layer issues, middleboxes, or silent data corruption—don't assume L2 CRC catches all end-to-end faults

questions.question: Route summarization helps when:
options: It reduces table size and hides churn—but can create blackholes if specifics disappear underneath
